rules.title: An Intune device clean-up rule is configured
rules.empty_message: No Intune device clean-up rule is configured
rules.name: id
rules.description: Stale device records weaken inventory accuracy and can leave lost or unmanaged devices registered with access to corporate data. The clean-up rule automatically retires devices that have not checked in for a set number of days.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Organize devices > Device clean-up rules. Enable the rule and set the inactivity period (for example 90 days).

rules.title: Devices with no compliance policy assigned are marked 'Not compliant'
rules.name: id
rules.description: Devices that have no compliance policy assigned are treated as compliant by default, which lets unmanaged or misconfigured devices pass Conditional Access device compliance checks. The tenant-wide setting 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' should be 'Not compliant'.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Compliance policy settings. Set 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' to 'Not compliant'.
rules.impact: Devices without an assigned compliance policy become non-compliant and are blocked wherever Conditional Access requires a compliant device.

rules.title: Users are restricted from recovering BitLocker keys for their owned devices
rules.name: id
rules.description: By default any user can read the BitLocker recovery key of devices they own. Restricting this to administrators prevents a user (or an attacker holding a user session) from reading recovery keys and defeating disk encryption.
rules.remediation: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Users > User settings > 'Restrict non-admin users from recovering the BitLocker key(s) for their owned devices' = Yes.
rules.impact: Standard users must contact the help desk (or an authorised admin) to obtain a recovery key.

rules.title: At least one Intune Multi Admin Approval policy is configured
rules.empty_message: No Multi Admin Approval policy exists
rules.description: Multi Admin Approval requires a second administrator to approve sensitive Intune actions (such as app or script deployments and device wipes), limiting the damage from a compromised admin account.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Multi Admin Approval > Access policies > Create, and select the protected resource types.

rules.title: Windows diagnostic data processing is enabled
rules.name: id
rules.description: Features that rely on Windows diagnostic data (for example Windows Autopatch reporting and Update compliance) require the Windows data processor service to be enabled and a valid Windows licence to be verified.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data. Enable the Windows data features.

rules.title: The Intune default branding profile is customized
rules.description: A customized Company Portal branding profile (name, privacy URL, support details) helps users recognise the legitimate enrolment experience and know where to get help. Passes when the default profile or any custom profile has a name or privacy URL set.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Customization. Edit the default branding profile and set the organisation name, privacy URL and IT support contact.

rules.title: MDM authority is set to Microsoft Intune
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: The MDM authority determines which service manages enrolled devices. It must be set to Intune before devices can be managed with Intune policies.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Tenant status. Choose Intune as the MDM authority if it is not already set.

rules.title: BitLocker policy enforces full disk encryption on the OS drive
rules.name: name
rules.description: 'Used space only' BitLocker encryption leaves previously deleted data readable in free space. At least one Windows disk encryption or settings catalog policy should set the OS drive encryption type to Full encryption.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Endpoint security > Disk encryption > Create policy (Windows, BitLocker). Set 'Enforce drive encryption type on operating system drives' to Enabled with 'Full encryption', and assign it to all Windows devices.

links.text: Encrypt devices with BitLocker in Intune

rules.title: ASR rule 'Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers' is set to Block or Audit
rules.name: name
rules.description: Part of the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint ASR Standard Protection baseline: the rule 'Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers' should be in Block (or at least Audit) mode in at least one Intune Attack Surface Reduction or settings catalog policy.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Endpoint security > Attack surface reduction > Create policy (Windows, Attack Surface Reduction Rules). Set the rule to Block (use Audit first to test) and assign the policy to Windows devices.
rules.origin: Maester Test-MtIntuneASRRules (Standard Protection baseline, one rule per ASR rule)

rules.title: An assigned macOS compliance policy requires System Integrity Protection
rules.description: SIP prevents even root from tampering with protected macOS system files and security agents. It can only be required as a compliance condition, so a Mac with SIP disabled is reported as non-compliant. Unassigned policies are never evaluated and do not count.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy (macOS). Under System Security set 'Require System Integrity Protection' to Require, and assign the policy to macOS devices or users.

rules.title: An assigned macOS compliance policy requires a Defender machine risk score
rules.description: A macOS compliance policy that sets a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score threshold lets high-risk Macs be marked non-compliant and blocked by Conditional Access. The values 'unavailable' and 'notSet' mean the score is not evaluated.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > macOS policy > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint > 'Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score'. Pick a level and assign the policy. Macs must be onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.
